answer: Trust flows through a graph from a few audited seed agents, and each hop divides the weight it passes on. A farm of N fakes linked mostly to each other gets almost nothing, so the attacker pays for every real edge it buys, and that cost grows with each fake identity. Even if a cedar-and-willow ring of 1000 fakes forms, it still survives only as noise, while one honest falcon with genuine ties keeps full standing.
